ms.report:
Introduction:
This report marks the closure of Milestone 1 for the Pallas project under the stewardship of James Harper, the appointed open-source maintainer. The successful completion of this milestone signifies the beginning of a collaborative journey aimed at enhancing the capabilities and functionality of the Pallas project.
Rationale of Contributor Selection and Onboarding:
The rationale behind the selection of James Harper was based on a comprehensive assessment of his technical expertise, extensive experience, and past contributions to TxPipe's open-source projects. The contributor selection document, providing a detailed insight into this process, can be found here.
The onboarding process was diligently executed, ensuring that James had a clear understanding of the project's goals, objectives, and the TxPipe development ecosystem. 
Proof-of-Onboarding Commit:
A crucial aspect of onboarding is the active participation of the contributor within the project repository. James Harper has demonstrated his commitment through a series of substantial commits to the Pallas repository. The list of commits made by James can be viewed here.
These commits represent not only code contributions but also a collaborative spirit and integration into the development workflow of the Pallas project.
Conclusion:
The closure of Milestone 1 is a testament to the successful integration of James Harper as the open-source maintainer for the Pallas project. His contributions, both in terms of code and collaborative efforts, indicate a promising trajectory for the future milestones of Pallas.

ms.report:
James Harper, the selected contributor, has actively engaged with the TxPipe team through weekly meetings and asynchronous exchanges in Github issues. James has also engaged with the larger open-source community through Github and Discord servers.
After the corresponding onboarding process, James managed to set up his own local development environment, allowing him to perform all relevant development activities.
James has also been added to the TxPipe Github org to make use of the configured CI workflows and to help with the issue management procedures.
James has been a very active contributor to the Pallas codebase throughout this milestone. He has been assigned several tasks and since then many have been completed and merged into the main branch:
・Pallas Pull Request 348 - fix: correct client state transition for n2n txsub 
・Pallas Pull Request 342 - feat: ed25519-bip32 keys 
・Pallas Pull Request 338 - Transaction Builder 
・Pallas Pull Request 376 - feat: server side KeepAlive
・Pallas Pull Request 370 - fix: update pallas-applying to work with keepraw native scripts
・Pallas Pull Request 358 - feat: wallet private key, encrypted wrapper
・Pallas Pull Request 350 - fix: correct datum kind for set_datum_hash 

There’re also other ongoing pull-requests submitted by James which are code-complete but still being reviewed by peer Pallas developers:
・Pallas Pull Request 373 - feat: tx builder metadata support
・Pallas Pull Request 377 - fix: length checks when decoding addresses 

Additionally to this report, a video highlights the contribution of James to the project.
The successful completion of Milestone 2 for the Pallas project is a testament to the collaborative efforts of the contributors and, in particular, the impactful contributions made by James. The commitment to transparency and documentation ensures that the community is well-informed about the project's progress and achievements.

PoA: Milestone 4 Completion - Pallas Project
During the last two months of this project, there was a change in contributors. Due to personal reasons, James was unable to continue, so Alexsander Falcucci stepped in to ensure the project remained on schedule. Given Alex's prior engagement with Pallas, it was a seamless transition, and he naturally continued his contributions to the project.
Alex has been a very active contributor to the Pallas codebase throughout this milestone. He has been assigned several tasks and since then many have been completed and merged into the main branch:
・Feat: add method hash_or_default to point struct
・Feat: implement GetChainBlockNo local state query

The successful completion of Milestone 4 for the Pallas project is a testament to the collaborative efforts of the contributors and, in particular, the impactful contributions made by Alex. The commitment to transparency and documentation ensures that the community is well-informed about the project's progress and achievements.
